pages.title: Meet Apache Kafka: The Event Streaming Backbone
bulletPoints: Kafka is a distributed, horizontally scalable, fault-tolerant, commit-log based event streaming platform.
Evolution: Created at LinkedIn to replace brittle point-to-point data pipelines with a unified publish/subscribe log.
High-throughput architecture: Capable of handling millions of messages per second with constant time O(1) performance.
Persistence by design: Messages are written durably to disk and replicated across cluster nodes before acknowledgment.
pages.footerText: Page 1 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide

pages.title: Core Primitives: Messages, Keys, and Schemas
bulletPoints: Message structure: An immutable payload consisting of an optional key, value, timestamp, and optional headers.
Message keys: Used for partitioning; records with identical keys are guaranteed to route to the same partition in order.
Schema evolution: Enforcing data contracts with Schema Registry (Avro, Protobuf, JSON Schema) prevents producer regressions.
Batched compression: Producers compress batches of records (Snappy, zstd, lz4, gzip) for optimal network efficiency.
pages.footerText: Page 2 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide

pages.title: Topics, Partitions, and the Append-Only Commit Log
bulletPoints: A Topic is a logical category of feeds to which records are published (e.g. `order-placed` or `user-signups`).
Partitions are the fundamental unit of parallelism: A topic is divided into one or more ordered, immutable partition logs.
Strict ordering guarantee: Records are totally ordered within a single partition, assigned a sequential offset number.
Horizontal scale: Partitions are distributed across multiple brokers, allowing read and write throughput to scale linearly.
pages.formulaOrSummary: Topic = Collection of Partitions [P0, P1, P2...]
pages.footerText: Page 3 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide

pages.title: Producer Architecture: Internals of send()
bulletPoints: The producer send() call does not immediately transmit over the network; it serializes and enqueues to RecordAccumulator.
RecordAccumulator organizes memory buffers by partition, grouping individual messages into batches.
Sender thread: A dedicated background I/O thread drains batches and transmits batched socket requests to broker leaders.
Batching parameters: `batch.size` (max bytes per batch) and `linger.ms` (wait time to allow fuller batch formation).
pages.footerText: Page 4 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide

pages.title: Producer Configuration: acks, retries, and Idempotence
bulletPoints: `acks=0`: Producer does not wait for broker response; maximum throughput, but highest risk of data loss.
`acks=1`: Producer waits for partition leader to write locally; balances latency and durability.
`acks=all` (or -1): Producer waits for all In-Sync Replicas (ISR) to acknowledge; maximum durability guarantee.
`enable.idempotence=true`: Assigns a Producer ID (PID) and sequence numbers to eliminate duplicate writes upon retries.
pages.footerText: Page 5 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide

pages.title: Custom Partitioners: Traffic Distribution
bulletPoints: Default partitioner: Hashes the record key using MurmurHash2 to deterministically select the partition.
Round-robin partitioner: Evenly spreads keyless records across all partitions to prevent hotspotting.
Sticky partitioner: Fills one partition batch completely before switching to the next, optimizing compression on keyless records.
Custom partitioner: Implement custom routing logic (e.g. route VIP tenant traffic to dedicated high-performance partitions).
pages.footerText: Page 6 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide

pages.title: Consumer Architecture & Consumer Groups
bulletPoints: Consumer Groups: Enable scalable, parallel consumption of topic partitions across multiple consumer instances.
Partition assignment rule: Each partition within a topic is consumed by exactly one consumer within a given consumer group.
Scaling limit: Having more consumers than topic partitions means idle consumers; partition count caps consumer concurrency.
Multiple groups: Distinct consumer groups read independently at their own pace without affecting each other.
pages.footerText: Page 7 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide

pages.title: Consumer Rebalance Protocol & Sticky Rebalancing
bulletPoints: Rebalance trigger: Consumers joining, leaving, crashing, or topic partition counts changing triggers a partition rebalance.
Group Coordinator: One Kafka broker acts as coordinator managing heartbeats and group membership.
Eager rebalance: All consumers revoke their partitions and pause consumption while assignments are recalculated.
Cooperative Sticky Rebalance: Consumers retain non-conflicting partitions and only transfer migrating partitions seamlessly.
pages.footerText: Page 8 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide

pages.title: Offsets and Commits: Guaranteeing Delivery
bulletPoints: Consumer offset: An integer pointing to the next record the consumer expects to read from that partition.
Auto-commit (`enable.auto.commit=true`): Periodically commits offsets; simple, but risks data loss or duplication on crash.
Manual commit (`commitSync` / `commitAsync`): Commit offsets only after downstream business logic successfully executes.
Storage: Committed offsets are stored in an internal, compacted system topic named `__consumer_offsets`.
pages.footerText: Page 9 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide

pages.title: The Broker Architecture & Metadata Management
bulletPoints: A Kafka Cluster is composed of multiple broker nodes communicating over TCP.
Leader and followers: For every partition, one broker is the designated leader handling all reads and writes.
Followers act as replicas: Continuously fetching messages from the leader to keep their copy in sync.
Metadata propagation: Brokers share partition metadata so any client can discover the leader for any partition.
pages.footerText: Page 10 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide

pages.title: KRaft: Eliminating ZooKeeper with Raft Consensus
bulletPoints: Historical ZooKeeper: Managed cluster metadata externally, leading to split-brain risks and metadata sync bottlenecks.
KRaft (Kafka Raft Metadata Mode): Replaces ZooKeeper by embedding metadata directly into an event-driven Raft quorum.
Instant cluster recovery: KRaft metadata is stored as an internal Kafka topic, enabling near-instantaneous controller failover.
Scalability boost: Supports millions of partitions per cluster with sub-second controller switchovers.
pages.formulaOrSummary: Legacy: Kafka + ZooKeeper ====> Modern: KRaft Unified Consensus
pages.footerText: Page 11 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide

pages.title: Replication: Leaders, Followers & In-Sync Replicas (ISR)
bulletPoints: Replication factor (RF): Specifies how many copies of each partition exist across distinct brokers (RF=3 is standard).
In-Sync Replicas (ISR): The subset of replicas that are actively caught up with the leader’s log.
`replica.lag.time.max.ms`: If a follower falls behind for longer than this duration, it is dropped from the ISR.
Clean leader election: By default, only members of the ISR can be elected as the new leader if the current leader dies.
pages.footerText: Page 12 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide

pages.title: High Watermark & Log End Offset (LEO)
bulletPoints: Log End Offset (LEO): The offset of the very next record that will be written to the local partition log.
High Watermark (HW): The highest offset that has been successfully replicated to all In-Sync Replicas.
Consumer visibility: Consumers can only read messages up to the High Watermark to prevent reading uncommitted data.
Truncation on recovery: Replicas recovering from an outage truncate their uncommitted logs back to the High Watermark.
pages.footerText: Page 13 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide

pages.title: Physical Storage: Log Segments & Zero-Copy I/O
bulletPoints: Partition logs are split physically into Log Segments (e.g. 1GB files: `000000.log`, `000000.index`, `000000.timeindex`).
Memory-mapped indexes: Sparse index files map offsets to physical file positions for lightning-fast binary searches.
Sequential disk I/O: Append-only disk writes bypass random head seeks, achieving sustained drive saturation speeds.
Zero-Copy optimization: Uses the `sendfile()` OS system call to transfer bytes from page cache directly to network socket.
pages.footerText: Page 14 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide

pages.title: Log Compaction: Key-Value Snapshots & Tombstones
bulletPoints: Log compaction retains at least the latest value for each message key within a topic indefinitely.
Log Cleaner: Background cleaner threads scan older segments and purge obsolete records that have newer updates.
Tombstones: Writing a record with a key and a `null` value acts as a tombstone, signaling permanent deletion after a grace period.
Use cases: Replicating database change data capture (CDC) tables, caching user account balances, and application config.
pages.footerText: Page 15 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide

pages.title: Reliable Message Delivery Guarantees
bulletPoints: Broker reliability recipe: Replication factor >= 3, `min.insync.replicas=2`, and `unclean.leader.election.enable=false`.
Producer reliability recipe: `acks=all`, `retries=MAX_INT`, and `enable.idempotence=true`.
Consumer reliability recipe: Manual offset commits after business logic completion, or idempotent consumer data sinks.
Result: Complete end-to-end guarantee that zero data is dropped or duplicated during hardware and network crashes.
pages.footerText: Page 16 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide

pages.title: Transactional Messaging: Multi-Partition Atomicity
bulletPoints: Transactional API: Enables atomic writes across multiple topics and partitions within a single `beginTransaction()` block.
Read-Process-Write cycle: Read an event from an input topic, transform it, write to output, and commit input offset atomically.
Transaction Coordinator: A designated broker managing two-phase commit logs and writing marker messages to partitions.
Consumer isolation level: Set `isolation.level=read_committed` so consumers only see successfully committed transactions.
pages.footerText: Page 17 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide

pages.title: Kafka Connect: Source and Sink Ecosystem
bulletPoints: Kafka Connect is a scalable, fault-tolerant framework for integrating external datastores with Kafka without custom code.
Source Connectors: Continuously stream data from databases (Debezium CDC, PostgreSQL, MySQL) into Kafka topics.
Sink Connectors: Stream records from Kafka topics into downstream analytics sinks (Elasticsearch, Snowflake, S3, BigQuery).
Declarative configuration: Connectors are deployed and scaled via simple JSON REST API configurations.
pages.footerText: Page 18 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide

pages.title: Schema Registry: Data Governance & Compatibility
bulletPoints: Schema Registry stores versioned schemas (Avro, JSON Schema, Protobuf) independently from the payload messages.
Payload efficiency: Messages only carry a 4-byte Schema ID in their header rather than the complete schema schema string.
Compatibility enforcement: Backward, forward, and full compatibility validation blocks breaking schema changes at runtime.
Decoupled teams: Upstream producer teams can safely evolve schemas without crashing downstream consumer pipelines.
pages.footerText: Page 19 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide

pages.title: Kafka Streams: Embedded Stream Processing DSL
bulletPoints: Client library, not a cluster: Kafka Streams is an embedded Java library running directly inside standard microservices.
Core abstractions: KStream (record stream), KTable (changelog table), and GlobalKTable (broadcast lookup cache).
State stores: Uses local RocksDB instances to maintain state for stateful joins, aggregations, and windowing.
Interactive queries: Microservices can query local RocksDB state stores directly via REST without hitting external databases.
pages.footerText: Page 20 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide

pages.title: MirrorMaker 2 & Multi-Cluster Replication
bulletPoints: MirrorMaker 2 (MM2): Built on Kafka Connect to replicate topics across geographical regions and disaster recovery clusters.
Active-Passive replication: Production writes to primary cluster; secondary DR cluster mirrors topics in real time.
Active-Active architectures: Bi-directional replication with topic prefixing (e.g. `us-east.orders`, `eu-west.orders`).
Offset translation: MM2 translates consumer group offsets between clusters to enable seamless consumer failover.
pages.footerText: Page 21 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide

pages.title: Security: Encryption, Authentication, and ACLs
bulletPoints: Encryption in transit: SSL/TLS encryption for all client-broker and inter-broker communication.
Authentication: Mutual TLS (mTLS), SASL/PLAIN, SASL/SCRAM, and SASL/Kerberos (GSSAPI) identify client principals.
Authorization: Access Control Lists (ACLs) grant read, write, or describe permissions on specific topics and groups.
Audit logging: Track every access attempt and unauthorized connection to meet enterprise security compliance standards.
pages.footerText: Page 22 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide

pages.title: Monitoring Kafka: Critical Cluster Metrics
bulletPoints: Under-Replicated Partitions (URP): The most critical broker metric; indicates partitions where replicas have fallen behind.
Consumer Lag: The difference between latest partition offset and consumer current offset; indicates processing delays.
Offline Partitions: Partitions with no active leader; requires immediate human intervention.
JVM & OS metrics: Page cache hit ratio, disk I/O utilization, garbage collection pauses, and network socket buffer drops.
pages.footerText: Page 23 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide

pages.title: Performance Tuning: OS, Page Cache & Network
bulletPoints: Linux Page Cache: Kafka relies on the OS page cache for lightning caching; never set JVM heap larger than 32GB.
Disk subsystem: Use SSDs or NVMe drives configured with RAID 10 or JBOD; avoid RAID 5 due to parity write penalties.
Network threads: Tune `num.network.threads` and `num.io.threads` to match the CPU core count on the broker.
Socket buffer sizing: Increase `send.buffer.bytes` and `receive.buffer.bytes` for high-throughput 10GbE network interfaces.
pages.footerText: Page 24 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide

pages.title: Production Checklist & Disaster Recovery Best Practices
bulletPoints: Hardware sizing: Minimum 3 brokers across 3 availability zones for high availability quorum survivability.
Topic partition hygiene: Aim for no more than 4,000 partitions per broker to avoid file descriptor and memory overhead.
Graceful shutdown: Enable `controlled.shutdown.enable=true` to migrate partition leaders cleanly before node reboots.
Disaster drills: Regularly practice broker failure, disk replacement, and controller failover in staging environments.
pages.footerText: Page 25 of 25 · Kafka: The Definitive Guide
